People have different opinions about Indiana’s new law about religious freedom. Some people are strong against the law, because they believe it allows discrimination against gay people. Others, like Indiana’s Governor Mike Pence, are surprised by the anger. they say the law is just like other laws already in place. Some fans of Lucille Ball want her statue to be removed from a park in her hometown. They say that the statue looks ugly and does not do justice to the "I Love Lucy" star. The life-size bronze statue in Celoron, New York, has been compared to the snake from "Betlejuice" and actor Steve Buscemi, among other unflattering comparisons. Even Mayor Scott Schrecengost has gone on record saying he does not care for the statue, which shows the comic star holding a bottle of fictional nutrition elixir Vitameatavegamin. And yet, it has been a tourist draw since 209 for Celoron, the comedian's birthplace, attracting visitors who pose with the statue for pictures.

Muhammadu Buhari was Nigeria’s leader for the past before, he came to power by a military force. Now, he came to power through the votes. These are five reasons why one of the most fiercely contested elections in the country's history is so important. For the first time in Nigeria's history, the opposition party defeated the ruling party in democratic elections. Muhammadu Buhari, 72, won Nigeria's presidential election, defeating incumbent Goodluck Jonathan by about two million votes. Nigeria is significant because it is the biggest economy and most populous country in Africa; it is also one of Africa's largest oil producers and is a major supplier of crude oil to the United States.

People online and in the streets were very happy. They would think that Iran had won the World Cup. But this event is much bigger. Young people waved flags from their roofts, played music loudly from their cars, and chated online with the hashtag #IranTalks. The excitement came after a important nuclear deal with the United States and other world powers. This deal promises to end Iran's international isolation under years of crippling sanctions. Just before midnight on Thursday, Vali Asr street, one of Tehran's main streets, turned into something like a block party. Car horns blared. Men danced in the middle of traffic. Some people flaunted U. dollar bills.

A federal court in Brooklyn has charged a fourth man in a plot to providing support to terrorists and for some of the men to join ISIS. Dilkhayot Kasimov was added to a new indictment. This is the case of three men who were arrested earlier: Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. These three men were charged with two counts of providing support to a foreign terrorist organization. They have pleaded not guilty. It is unclear if Kasimov has been arrested.

The last lunar eclipse of a four series was the shortest one, but still a good thing for early risers in North America. The moon slipped fully into Earth's shadow at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. ET) Saturday, starting a total lunar eclipse for nearly five minutes -- what NASA says will be the shortest such eclipse of the century. The celestial body took on a burnt-orange tint in the minutes before, during and after the total eclipse, giving the moon the appearance that earns total eclipses the "blood moon" nickname.

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN) – On Tuesday, many people in Turkey were worried. “What is what happening? Why can I get into the subway?” asked an elderly woman wearing a white headscarf, holding several shopping bags. She was standing outside a blocked entrance at one of Istanbul’s busiest subway stations. She was one of millions of Turks who were confused and worried by the worst power outage to grip the country in more than a decade. Dozens of cities across Turkey lost power for hours on Tuesday. Millions of people were affected, including passengers stranded on paralyzed trains and subways.

California has new laws. Governor Jerry Brown on Wednesday imposed mandatory water restrictions for the first time on residents, businesses and farms, ordering cities and towns in the drought-ravaged state to reduce usage by 25%. "We're in a new era," Brown said. "The idea of your nice little green grass getting lots of water every day, that's going to be a thing of the past." The 25% cut in usage amounts to roughly 1.5 million acre-feet of water (an acre foot of water equals about 325,000 gallons) over the next nine months, state officials said.

Police in Australia have arrested two people after the 55 dead dogs were found in the Queensland bush. According to Australian media reports, the bodies were being dumped. One of the people arrested was a licensed greyhound trainer. The other two people are residents of Bundaberg, a 7-year-old man and a 6-year-old woman. Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their Wisconsin town. They successfully selling their frozen pizzas, including breakfast pizzas and gluten-free options, in stores across Nichols, west of Green Bay. They built a base of loyal customers. But all that was threatened this week when people began misting them for Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana, which made national headlines after its owners said they would refuse to cater a same-sex wedding. People posted angry comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza's Facebook page and called its phone number to protest.

A complete camel skeleton has been found under a cellar in Austria. It was used by Ottoman troops during the 17th century. The remains were uncovered by archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni), exploring the construction site for a shopping center in the city of Tulln in 2006-2007. "The partly excavated skeleton was at first suspected to be a large horse or cattle," archaeozoologist Alfred Galik said. "But one look at the cervical vertebrae, the lower jaw and the metacarpal bones immediately revealed that this was a camel."

Andrew Getty, 47, died on Tuesday in his home in Los Angeles. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, confirmed the death. They said the family asks that the media and public respect their privacy during this difficult time. The death "appe to be natural causes or an accident," Ed Winter, assistant chief in the Los Angeles County coroner's office, told CNN affiliate KTLA Tuesday night. Some medication had also been recovered from Getty's home, though investigators don't know if Getty was currently taking it or what his medical history was, Winter said.

The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 into the French Alps on March 24, killing everyone on board. The latest report shows that he sped up the descent of the plane to its doom. It's terrifying. How much did his battle with depression affect his fitness to fly? Should he have walked away from his job? Should his doctors have sounded alarm bells? His case raises larger and important issues about people who are burdened with mental illness and the pressure of its stigma.

CNN – He didn’t want to give his name, but the tattoo on his neck— “Gertrude”” gave him away. That’s what Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said on Saturday about Kamron Taylor, the 23-year-old convicted murderer turned jail escapee until his arrest overnight in Chicago. Authorities around Illinois had been looking for Taylor since early Wednesday, when he jumped a correctional officer at Kankakee’s Jerome Combs Detention Center, then took off with the guard’s uniform and SUV. Surveillance video was the last officials saw of Taylor until just before midnight Friday, in Chicago. “They saw a guy that matched the description,” Bukowski said.

Prince Harry, who is 30 years, from Britain, is going to spend some time with the Australian military. He will arrive in Australia on Monday for a four-week stay. The Australian Defence Forces said on Thursday that Harry will work and live with soldiers in several units in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. He has already spent time with Australian troops on a number of occasions during his 10-year military career, a spokesman said.

Two Florida prison guards and a former guard trainee are charged in a plot to kill a former inmate who was getting out of prison, the Florida Attorney General’s office said Thursday.

An FBI informant met the men—Thomas Jordan Driver, 25; David Elliot Moran, 47; and Charles Thomas Newcomb, 42— after infiltrating a branch of the KKK: the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, CNN affiliate WJXT reported. Driver told the informant that he had gotten into a fight with the inmate and that he and Moran wanted him "six feet under," according to court documents.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A long and difficult series of talks ended on Thursday in Lausanne. The group of world powers, known as the P5+1, reached a framework agreement with Iran regarding its nuclear program. The success of this agreement is still being tested. The parties have until the end of June to work out the details and put the plan into writing. But the talks this week were, nevertheless, historic, especially for the otherwise frozen U-US-I relationship. But that's not to say they were glamorous. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

On Monday morning, an improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle near the Somali city of Garowe. The explosion killed six people, including four aid workers for UNICEF. Somalia’s President said the attack was “an attack against the future of our country.”. The attack happened about 8 a.m. in the administrative capital of the autonomous Puntland region. The terrorist group Al-Shabab claimed responsibility for the attack. The United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia confirmed this. The attack follows a separate incident Sunday in which three African Union troops died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia.

Prince Harry of Britain arrived in Australia on Monday. He will stay there for four weeks to working with the Australian military. Before his first day, the 30-year-old prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. A crowd of onlookers gathered outside the memorial. Some snapped photos of the royal visitor, while one boy held a sign celebrating the prince's hair color: "Red Heads Rule!" During his time down under, Harry "will work and live alongside colleagues in the Australian Army in a number of regiments in Sydney, Darwin and Perth," the Australian Defence Forces said last week.

Australia, a important ally of the United States, has agreed to share some of its intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the deal is "an informal arrangement" with an emphasis on tracking Australians who go to Iraq to fight for ISIS. But one Australian lawmaker reportedly described the move as "dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in 2 years, meeting with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview released Monday that Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Tehran.

French investigators have early findings from the flight data recorder, which was recovered from the Germanwings Flight 9525. The data shows that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally used the controls to make the plane descend faster. The flight data recorder, also known as the "black box," was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had been searching the mountainside in the French Alps since the March 24 crash. The plane went down there. The BEA, the French air accident investigation agency, stated on Friday that its teams immediately started investigating the contents of the recorder.

A 110-day chase between ships between the Antarctic waters and the west African coast ended with an unusual way when the crew of a alleged poaching vessel were rescued by conservationists pursuing them. Environmentalist group Sea Shepherd had been tailing the Thunder -- subject of an Interpol "purple notice" for suspected fraud and fisheries-related crimes -- since its ship the Bob Barker encountered it in the Southern Ocean several months ago. The pursuit ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of west Africa, when the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

Saudi state media reported that a Saudi border guard was killed in Yemen. This is the first death that Saudi Arabia has publicly confirmed during its military campaign against rebels in neighboring Yemen. The incident happened on Wednesday night in Asir, southwestern Saudi Arabia. The Saudi Press Agency (SPA) reported that militants in a mountainous area of Yemen fired on Saudi border troops. The Saudi troops returned fire. The guard, identified as Cpl. Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki, was killed. 10 others were injured, but their injuries were not life-threatening.

I feel nervous as I go to the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. The camel owners are sitting on the floor, eating the a'ish, a traditional Arabic dish of fish and rice, laid out in front of them. The conversation is loud and exciting.

It may not be as fast or luxurious as a Ferrari or a Rolls Royce, but the humble hatchback is now 50 years old. The car shape originally designed to help French farmers transport their sheep to market now accounts for a staggering two in every three cars sold in the UK. And it is just as popular across the world from Munich to Mexico City thanks to its practical design, economy and comfort. The model credited with being the world’s first ever hatchback was the Renault 16 unveiled in April 1965. The Renault 4: the forerunner to the Renault 16 was first designed to allow French farmers to transport sheep.

With only seconds left in the game, Arango went up to Zavala and bit him on the shoulder. Arango, who is 34 years old, said, "I did something I shouldn't have done with Zavala." The video shows Arango biting Zavala's shoulder. Zavala held his shoulder after being bitten by Arango. Zavala's team won 4-3. Zavala showed the referee the mark on his shoulder after being bitten by Arango.

Almeria, a team in Spain’s lower division, has appointed Sergi Barjuan as their new head coach. Barjuan, 43, is the third manager this season. He replaces Juan Ignacio Martinez, who was fired on Sunday after Almeria lost 4-1 to Levante. Barjuan will manage Almeria’s away game against Barcelona on Wednesday, once all paperwork is complete. Barjuan, a former Barcelona defender, played 53 times for Spain between 1998 and 2004. He played for Barcelona for nine years and appeared in two World Cups for Spain. He managed Recreativo in Spain’s second division from 2012 to 2014.

Arsene Wenger hasn't decided if he will offer Abou Diaby a new contract, but he suggested that the French midfielder, who has been recovering from injuries, might stay at Arsenal after this summer. Diaby returned to play in a practice game on Wednesday, but he has only played in 22 games in the last five years at the Emirates Stadium, because of his injuries. Arsenal plays Liverpool on Saturday, and Wenger probably won't put Diaby in a important game, since both teams are in important seasons, but he said Diaby might get a new deal, possibly with a pay-as-you-play deal.

The golf tournament in Houston, the Shell Houston Open, is happening without Tiger Woods or Rory McIlroy. But it doesn’t seem to be a problem. The city of Humble, where the event is held, is seeing record numbers of attendance. This is the last tournament before the Masters, and it has been very successful thanks to the crowd-pleing antics of the popular Phil Mickelson and local boy Jordan Spieth. It’s 18 months now since Spieth attracted criticism for giving up on university and joining the PGA Tour as the 809th ranked player in the world. Spieth, only 21, has since risen to number four in the world. Funnly enough, no-one’s criticing him anymore.
